bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v1, April 7 2024; submitted for Meta internal review March 14, 2024)

question: How many bits of factual knowledge can a language model store per parameter, and how do training duration, architecture, quantization, MoE sparsity and junk data change that capacity?
hypothesis: Knowledge storage scales linearly with parameters with a universal constant that can be measured on controlled synthetic data (stated implicitly: 'does the total knowledge scale linearly with the model's size? What is the exact constant?').
contributions: A framework (bit-complexity lower bound, Theorem 3.2, and capacity ratio R(F)) that measures knowledge bits stored by a model on synthetic (name, attribute, value) data
12 results: 2 bits/param after 1000 exposures, 1 bit/param at 100 exposures, architecture, int8/int4 quantization, MoE, and junk data effects
Mitigation: prepend a special token (like a domain name) to useful data

method.summary: Pretrain GPT2 (rotary embeddings, no dropout), LLaMA, Mistral and variants from random initialization on synthetic biographies (bioS, bioSsimple, bioR) and a parameterised bioD dataset, sweeping model size and number of people N. Learned knowledge bits are computed from the summed cross-entropy loss on knowledge tokens via the Theorem 3.2 lower bound, and divided by parameter count to give the capacity ratio. Variations: 1000 vs 100 exposures, architecture, GPTQ int8/int4, 32-expert MoE, 7/8 junk tokens with or without a special token.
method.task: next-token pretraining on synthetic knowledge; capacity measurement

datasets.name: bioS(N)
datasets.size: N from 10K to 20M people (bioS(20M) about 1B bits); 6 attributes each, ~47.6 bits/person excluding names
datasets.split: none; knowledge learned is measured on the training people; extractability test fine-tunes on half of people, tests on other half
datasets.source: Synthetic, from Allen-Zhu and Li [3]; online generation: each biography freshly sampled from 50 sentence templates per attribute, random order
datasets.preprocessing: Paragraphs randomly concatenated with <EOS>, randomly cut into 512-token windows; GPT2Tokenizer (only 3275 distinct tokens used)

datasets.name: bioSsimple(N)
datasets.source: Each biography generated once with fixed template choice and order

datasets.name: bioR(N)
datasets.source: bioS facts each written 40 times by LLaMA2

datasets.name: bioD(N,K,C,D,L,T)
datasets.preprocessing: One paragraph per person, random attribute order, fixed template

datasets.name: Junk mixture
datasets.size: 1/8 of tokens bioS(N) useful (N 50K to 1M), 7/8 bioS(N'=100M) junk or N'=1K repetitive
datasets.preprocessing: Each 512-token window holds only useful or only junk data, separated by <EOS>

models.name: GPT2-l-h (rotary, no dropout)
models.params: 1M to 0.5B (bioS(N) base laws); GPT2-small counted as 88M
models.architecture: GPT-2 decoder with rotary position embedding, no dropout, tied embedding/output
models.layers: l, 1-layer models excluded from main figures; up to GPT2-28-20, GPT2-25-20, GPT2-20-16

models.name: LLaMA-l-h
models.architecture: gated MLP (silu), untied weights, LLaMA tokenizer, no layernorm bias, no GQA

models.name: Mistral-l-h
models.architecture: gated MLP with 10.5d^2 MLP params, group-query attention (4 groups if h%4==0, 1 if odd, else 2)

models.name: GPT2_1/4 and GPT2_0
models.architecture: GPT2 with MLP d->d->d (1/4 size) or no MLP

models.name: GPT2-MoE (32 experts)
models.architecture: MLP replaced by 32 experts d->d->d, tutel; topk=1, cap factor=2 (8 at test); total/effective params ratio ~11.3

training.lr: 0.0005 to 0.001 typical; per-N values in other (0.0002 to 0.005)
training.lr_schedule: cosine decay from 1 to 0.1 times the reference rate
training.precision: mixed-precision fp16 (bf16 for LLaMA/Mistral where fp16 unstable; GPT2 bf16 nearly identical)
training.wall_clock: 8.5 days (GPT2-20-16, bioS(10M), 1000 exposures, 64 A100s); 2.4 days (GPT2-12-32, bioS(20M), 100 exposures, hardware not stated)

other.LLaMA_Mistral: best of 3 learning rates per N; bf16 for 2M+ at 1000 exposures and for all 100-exposure runs
other.MoE: higher lrs, e.g. 1000 exposure N=10K lr .001/.002; 100 exposure 50K lr .001/.002/.005
other.junk: per-run wd/lr/batch in App E Parameter 10 (e.g. 100-exposure junk N=50K wd .01 lr .0003/.0005/.001 bs 12; 1000-exposure N=200K bs 1536)
other.gpus_irrelevant: Remark A.3: results same on 64 GPUs bs 24 or 1536 GPUs bs 1
other.exposures: 1000 or 100 (also 300/600 with junk); 100 exposures of bioR = 2.5 passes, 1000 = 25 passes

inference.prompting: Memorization test: prompt 'Anya Briar Forger was born on' and check generation; extractability: QA text 'What is the birthday of Anya Briar Forger? Answer: October 2, 1996.'

other.extractability_finetune: LoRA on half of people, ranks (r',r) in {(8,2),(16,2),(8,4),(32,4),(8,8),(32,8),(128,8),(32,16),(128,16)}, best reported; no warmup, bs 96, lr 0.001 linear decay to 0, wd 0.1, 75,000 steps

metrics.name: capacity ratio R(F)
metrics.definition: [N log2(N0/e^p1) + N log2(S0/e^p2)] / P for bioS (with an extra diversity term for bioD), p1 = summed loss on name tokens, p2 = summed loss on value tokens; P = parameters

metrics.name: max capacity ratio Rmax(F)
metrics.definition: bit complexity of the data (loss zero) divided by P

metrics.name: memorizable / extractable knowledge accuracy
metrics.definition: summed per-person accuracy over five attributes (company city excluded)

baselines: GPT2 vs LLaMA, Mistral, GPT2 with 1/4 MLP, no MLP, 32-expert MoE; no-junk vs junk
eval.protocol: Peak R(F) across a sweep of model shapes per N; positive results use one fixed lr set, negative results report the best of 3 lrs. No seeds or error bars stated.

limits: Synthetic, uniformly random (name, attribute, value) facts; real knowledge is not uniform and not measured; the 2 bits/param is for idealised data
Only exposures of 100 and 1000 for base laws; no exposure counts beyond 1000 without junk, and capacity law needs 1000 exposures to reach 2
Largest models only 0.5B params, GPT2 up to 28 layers; authors saw 'no need to scale up further'
Single quantization method (GPTQ via auto_gptq); authors say other methods unexplored; int4 result may reflect the package
Negative results use best-of-3 learning rates, positive results single lr sets (deliberate asymmetry)
Footnote 19 omitted experiment on layer-removal probing
Paper contains no analysis of membership inference, memorization of rare strings, or tokens-per-parameter thresholds

terms.definition: model's learned knowledge bits (Theorem 3.2 lower bound) divided by parameter count
each knowledge piece is visited N times during training, differing from N passes since one pass can expose a piece many times
minimum bits required to encode the N knowledge tuples
